primary_claim: Pre-trained base LLMs already refuse harmful requests (48% on average) via the same 'refusal direction' mechanism used by chat models in Qwen 1.5 0.5B and Gemma 2 9B, indicating chat fine-tuning reinforces existing refusal circuitry rather than learning it from scratch, whereas in LLaMA 1 7B the base and chat refusal mechanisms differ.

effect.metric: refusal rate on 100 JailbreakBench harmful instructions
effect.value: base models 48% avg vs chat models 90% avg; steering with refusal direction raises base refusal to over 88%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Contradicts the commonly assumed view (attributed to Arditi et al.) that refusal is a behavior developed exclusively during chat fine-tuning rather than pre-training

Qi et al. 2024 independently found (via correspondence) that Llama-2 7B base and Gemma-1 7B also refuse; authors note their work was therefore not first to establish the narrow claim that base models refuse, though their steering results and pre/post-ChatGPT comparison are novel
stated_future_work: More systematic analysis of how fine-tuning changes model internals, ideally at the low level of identifying how features and circuits have changed
Better understand refusal circuits, potentially using SAEs which recent tooling advances might make more tractable

Gain more insight into why the refusal ablation technique worked poorly on the LLaMA 1 base model, e.g. whether it has a separate 'incompetent refusal' direction needing different ablation data or method
limitations_stated: Only 3 models were investigated, and only one was purely trained with data before the release of ChatGPT
Base model generations can vary significantly based on small edits to the prompt, so exact base model refusal rates should not be over-indexed on

Lack of transparency into the pre-training of Qwen 1.5 0.5B and Gemma 2 9B; modern pre-training datasets may be filtered or contain synthetic data, which could blur the standard base vs chat model distinction
quote: we find that on average, base models already refuse 48% of harmful requests by default, just at a lower rate than their chat models (90%).
